Legacy plain-text keys are matched by DB equality Project.objects.get(api_key=...)/Q(...) (hc/accounts/models.py:422-439), not a constant-time comparison, unlike hashed keys (models.py:593); timing-only weakness, limited to legacy keys.

request.readonly = key.startswith('hcr_') or key == project.api_key_readonly (hc/api/decorators.py:87-89): a hashed hcr_ key is only matched on api_key_readonly (accounts/models.py:415-418, 582-583), a legacy read-only key equals api_key_readonly, and a rw key cannot satisfy either short of a legacy rw key starting with 'hcr_' (which would only be more restricted); no misclassification toward read-write.
_lookup starts from Check.objects.filter(project=project) (hc/api/views.py:300) with project = request.project (views.py:446), so it can only match the key's own project.

_update resolves channels only from Channel.objects.filter(project=check.project) (hc/api/views.py:323, 330), and check.project is the key's project (create: views.py:451; update: project check at 502).

update, pause, resume, pings, ping_body and channels use @authorize with accept_ro=False (hc/api/views.py:499, 546, 573, 595, 625, 473; decorators.py:59) and each per-check one compares project ids (views.py:502, 549, 576, 598, 628); channels filters by request.project (475).

get_check compares project (hc/api/views.py:483) and passes readonly (486); flips checks project (650) and returns only timestamps/up (models.py:1384+); badges uses request.project (695-698), and badge URLs are intended for read-only keys.
get_check_by_unique_key iterates request.project.check_set.all() (hc/api/views.py:493), so it can only return a check of the key's own project.

These are intended public endpoints authenticated by other secrets: badge needs a valid signature (hc/api/views.py:739), check_badge a random badge_key UUID (789), ping a check UUID (190), ping_by_slug the project ping_key (260), notification_status/bounces are webhooks (821, 887).

The API views authenticate only via an explicit API key (hc/api/decorators.py:49-61, 74-84), never session cookies, so wildcard CORS (decorators.py:112-113) and csrf_exempt let no foreign origin use a victim's ambient credentials.
The Prometheus metrics view resolves the project from the read-only key (hc/integrations/prometheus/views.py:50) and filters Check.objects.filter(project_id=project.id) (line 54).
